experiment: Track B validation: motion of a KNOWN asteroid in real SPHEREx exposures, checked against JPL Horizons
claim: none about new objects; this checks our detection, linking and astrometry on a body with a well-known orbit

spacecraft_check.what: |SPHEREx position in FITS header (X_SC,Y_SC,Z_SC, geocentric) - Horizons -163182 vector|

parallax_note: SPHEREx orbits ~650 km up (|r| ~ 7000 km from the geocentre). At the asteroid's distance this shifts it by up to 3.3 arcsec versus a geocentric ephemeris, with a 98-minute period. We therefore compare with Horizons evaluated AT SPHEREx (500@-163182); the geocentric residuals are listed only to show the size of the effect.

pipeline_flag_finding.what: exposures whose 2-px aperture at the Horizons position contains pixels flagged OUTLIER by the SPHEREx pipeline
pipeline_flag_finding.consequence: with the static-target mask (quality.BAD_PLANES) the asteroid is masked out; Track B keeps OUTLIER pixels

fitted_motion.model: polynomial of order 2 in (RA cos Dec, Dec) vs time, tangent plane at the field centre
fitted_motion.note: fit_rms and chi2_red measure the scatter about a smooth polynomial. The asteroid's path seen from SPHEREx also carries the orbital parallax (a few arcsec, 98-min period), which no low-order polynomial follows; the per-exposure residuals against Horizons evaluated AT SPHEREx are the astrometric test, the polynomial is only the motion summary.

time_shuffled_real_data.what: real detections, epoch times randomly permuted; Kleopatra's own detections lose their order too

time_shuffled_real_data_without_kleopatr.what: as above, with the detections linked to Kleopatra removed first

noise_only_fields.what: SIMULATED Gaussian noise drawn from each real VARIANCE plane, real flag mask and WCS, no sources

limitations: One asteroid, one 3.3-day window, one field. This shows the method works on a real case; it is not a survey-level completeness measurement.
Kleopatra was near its stationary point (rates of a few arcsec/hour), so the real test covers slow motion only; faster motion is covered by SIMULATED injections alone.
Centroids come from a fixed-width circular Gaussian, not the SPHEREx ePSF; SPHEREx pixels (6.15 arcsec) undersample the PSF, so sub-arcsec astrometry is not expected.

We keep pixels flagged OUTLIER (the pipeline marks the moving asteroid with it); other bad planes stay masked. Cosmic rays or artefacts flagged only as OUTLIER can therefore become detections; the false-positive tests include this.
Position errors are the formal fit errors scaled by sqrt(chi2_red); the field-star scatter is the better guide to the real floor.
SIMULATED sources are Gaussians without their own photon noise, injected into real cutouts; recovery is measured on this one field and cadence.

The time-shuffled test reuses this field's detections; it measures chance alignments among real transients, not every kind of false link. Such alignments are common at the 3-visit minimum, so a 3-visit track on its own is not evidence of a real mover in this field.
Linking assumes a polynomial path over the window; the SPHEREx orbital parallax (a few arcsec, 98-min period) is absorbed by the link tolerance, not modelled.

Tracks not matching Kleopatra were found. Each is listed with a JPL sb_ident lookup at its position; they are reported without interpretation (a slow 'track' can also come from a blended source whose centroid shifts with wavelength across detectors) and no new object is claimed.
